requiredFixes: Split paragraph 2 of H3 block 1 — isolate the list of added CTAs into one short paragraph, then make the interpretation ('this swap suggests...') its own standalone sentence or short paragraph, each under 60 words.

Rewrite the opening of H3 block 2 so the finding comes first — not the caveat about missing data. Lead with what the evidence confirms (CTA direction of travel), then acknowledge the nav-name limitation.

Cut or rephrase the closing sentence of H3 block 2 — replace 'consistent with that same direction' with a concrete implication: e.g., what a flat nav count alongside a CTA pivot typically signals about buyer journey design.
Add an immediate plain-language definition for 'self-serve content' in the same sentence it appears — e.g., 'self-serve content (pages a buyer can read without speaking to sales)'.

Trim paragraph 2 of H3 block 2 to under 60 words by removing the redundant phrase 'meaning steps a buyer takes when they are close to a decision, not still figuring out what the product does' — condense it into a clause, not a full parenthetical.

Rewrite the final sentence of the founder test to end on a concrete action, not a comparison — e.g., 'If person-to-proof skews toward person, replace one named-person CTA with a case study or demo link and note whether click-through changes within 30 days.'
riskFlags: The phrase 'your page may be structured differently from where Gong has moved' implies Gong's direction is the right direction — this is a soft causation claim without data support; hedge it explicitly.

'Suggests the page may now be built for someone who wants to evaluate on their own terms' — plausible inference but presented as near-fact; add a hedging qualifier such as 'one interpretation is' or 'the pattern is consistent with'.

'Bottom-of-funnel actions... steps a buyer takes when they are close to a decision' — characterising these five CTAs as bottom-of-funnel is an unsupported interpretive claim; 'See Gong in action' and 'Learn about our product' could equally serve mid-funnel visitors.

rewriteInstruction: Keep the evidence-grounded instinct of this draft — it correctly quotes every CTA verbatim, acknowledges data limits honestly, and avoids fabricating nav item names. Add a plain-language gloss for 'self-serve content' in the same sentence it appears, and soften the bottom-of-funnel characterisation of the added CTAs to avoid an unsupported causal claim.
